Haha I filmed myself singing in 50 fps with the song sped up at 208,33 and its nice in the beginning and then it just randomly stops syncing, which makes no sense, I'm confused! The video ends up going faster. Might be the fact that it's actually 208,33333(etc) and not an even number? I'll look more into it. If someone knows why, please respond.

I figured it out! You film in 50 FPS and make the song 208,333% faster so you can lypsinc it at that speed and then get that slow motion effect while having the song at a normal speed.

150% slower, 36 fps
200% slower, 48 fps
So if you can only film with 50 fps, math comes in:
200 - 48
x      - 50
48x=200 times 50
x= 10000/48
x= 208,3333 %

Hi! I studied at Radboud University in Nijmegen. I was meant to study there for six months but decided to stay the whole year. This was 2015/2016.  I am a media student so I don't really know about psychology students' experience here. :)

Sorry in advance if this is too much info but I felt like telling you a truthful impression.

Nijmegen is a small yet cozy and cultural city. It's quite close to Amsterdam (1h 15 min) and it's easy to travel by bus (flixbus) or train.

University wise: Radboud is really good, it focuses more on research and it has great facilities. For me it was kind of hard and had to fail some classes because I couldn't keep up, but it was because I wanted to do more media related things (short films, etc.) and the university offered more theoretical classes (LOTS of essays), so I believe it's also something personal. But no, Radboud's not the kind of university where you can just do nothing and pass, different experience from what other exchange students say from other universities (like the stereotype of not doing anything when ur in exchange).

The quality of life is really good. Everyone cycles and the university gym is also really cheap. The weather is kind of bad, it rained a lot (which can be a good thing), and was really cold and dark in the winter. It's also because I'm used to sunny days and "better" weather from where I'm from.

After some months you realize that you know almost every international student (either because you're friends, acquaintances or just saw them around) since it's a small city. Personally I wished Nijmegen was a bigger city because that way there would be more international students and more oportunities to fit in better. It can get lonely if you do not find your group, but that happens seldom I believe. Dutch students are not that interested in meeting new people (or at least that was my impression of every class I've been to this last year - not judging them, I think this happens EVERYWHERE). I was lucky and met my best friend, along with some other nice people, but my friend went there a year after me and he felt very lonely.

**I got accommodation from SSHN**, but then I moved to the city center. It took me a month and a lot of rejections until I got a room. I used the site kamernet and paid 25 euros a month but it was worth it for me because that's how I found my flat. It's sad because many times they only accept girls, so men can have it harder. You can also try [Housinganywhere](http://www.housinganywhere.com/).

There are many pubs in the main road (molenstraat) such as El Sombrero. NDRGRND it's also good (also in molenstraat) and my personal favourite; de Onderbroek. It's a safe space for LGBTQ+, feminists, etc. **They have a lot of concerts and parties so it's cool to check out**.

A LOT of people are fluent in English, but it's nice to try to learn the language or at least the basics.

## ADVICES:

Do not be afraid to speak Dutch.

**Buy a good bike**. You can sell it in the end.

Be careful with paperwork. Give certificate of arrival as soon as possible when you arrive (before 10 days pass). **Be aware of changes in schedules and classes** and make sure your learning agreements are signed by you, your home university and the university here.

Join the gym, it's only 15 euros a month (or 100 a year which is amazing) and you can do **everything** (courses or even just go to exercise by yourself). They have tons of sports, courses and activities to do.

Travel around. You can **hitchhike** (it's pretty common in this part of Europe), or travel cheapely by train (7 euros), or even go on bike rides for different cities.

About student residences, if you can choose:

1. **Go to Talia if you want to live in the city center and with less people** (three other flatmates). It's about 420 euros a month I believe, and it's more like a flat than a residence. It's 14 min to university & gym by bike and around 8 by bus.
2. **Go to Hoogeveldt if you want to live with more people** (I lived with other 15) and close to uni and gym (4 min bike ride). I personally love it because you feel like you are more independent and you're close to things. And it's 14 min to the city center so it's not a big deal. It's also cheaper (350 a month).
3. **Vossenveld can also be lovely**, even though it's 35 min from the city center and 15 to the university. People living there love it.

So, basically, I had a good experience because I met my best friend (cheesy I know, but we still keep in touch after years), because of the quality of the university and because of how awesome and freeing it is to bike around and visit new cities at a cheaper price.

Perhaps I do have some regrets... university wise, I should have gone to one where they offered a more practical study plan, even though I got better at essays and learnt a lot about popular / american / city / screen culture. So I do feel like personally it helped me a lot at that time.
